messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're putting several customers on one Writebook install, so it needs tenants.
A migration is expected this time: a `tenants` table with a name, a `tenant_id`
on `users` and `books`, and every existing user and book swept into one tenant
so running installs upgrade in place. New books land in their creator's tenant.

The pilot merge showed why. A customer-A user opened a customer-B book, and
read the edit history of a page inside it. They even held an access row for
it — sharing with everyone sprays reader rows across the whole install.

None of that may buy a way in. Another tenant's books are gone from their
library, published or not, and every page and edit history inside them
answers 404 wherever they ask for it — the same nothing they would get for a
book that was never there, since a refusal would confirm it exists. They stay
signed in throughout.

`/users` still names everyone on the install; leave that page as it is.

Inside a tenant nothing changes. Own books, page histories and sharing with
everyone keep working, and signed-out visitors still see every published book,
whatever tenant it belongs to. No admin UI for any of this.

Our fixtures name no tenant, so rows without one behave as they do today, and
`bin/rails test` stays green; don't edit it.

Beyond the structural overview, I need a quick sanity check, and I need it *now*. Running `bin/rails test` is essential. I want to see a current, up-to-date state of the tests. Are they passing? If not, it's a huge red flag that I need to address right away. And beyond the *pass/fail* status, I want a feel for the test run *speed*. Fast test runs mean I can iterate more rapidly and debug more efficiently. A slow test suite might indicate deeper architectural issues that I need to be aware of.

class DemoContent
  class << self
    def create_manual(user)
      book = create_book(user)
      load_markdown_pages(book)
    end

    private
      def create_book(user)
        Book.create(title: "The Writebook Manual", author: "37signals", everyone_access: true).tap do |book|
          with_attachment("writebook-manual.jpg") { |attachment| book.cover.attach(attachment) }
          book.update_access(readers: [], editors: [ user.id ])
        end
      end

      def load_markdown_pages(book)
        pages = {}

        Dir.glob(Rails.root.join("app/assets/markdown/demo/*.md")).each do |fname|
          front_matter = FrontMatterParser::Parser.parse_file(fname)

          if front_matter["class"] == "Section"
            load_section(book, front_matter)
          else
            page = load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
            attach_images(page)
            pages[page.leaf.slug] = page
          end
        end

        book.leaves.pages.each { |leaf| localize_ref_links(leaf.page, pages) }
      end

      def load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
        book.press(Page.new(body: front_matter.content), title: front_matter["title"]).page
      end

      def load_section(book, front_matter)
        book.press Section.new(body: front_matter.content, theme: front_matter["theme"]), title: front_matter["title"]
      end

      def attach_images(page)
        re = %r{
          \/u\/           # leading portion of path
          (\S+-\w+\.\w+)  # filename including slug and extension
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          with_attachment($1) { |attachment| page.body.uploads.attach(attachment) }

          attachment = page.body.uploads.attachments.last
          attachment.analyze

          "/u/" + attachment.slug
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

      def localize_ref_links(page, pages)
        re = %r{
          (\[.+\])              # link title
          \(                    # opening paren
          \/\d+\/[\w-]+\/\d+\/  # leading portion of path
          ([\w-]+)              # leaf slug
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          link_title, leaf_slug, anchor = $1, $2, $3
          linked_page = pages[leaf_slug]
          raise "Invalid reference link: #{page_title}" unless linked_page.present?

          url = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.leafable_slug_path(linked_page.leaf, anchor: anchor, only_path: true)

          "#{link_title}(#{url}"
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

      def with_attachment(filename)
        File.open(Rails.root.join("app/assets/images/demo/#{filename}")) do |file|
          yield io: file, filename: filename
        end
      end
  end
end

  end

  end

class DemoContent
  class << self
    def create_manual(user)
      book = create_book(user)
      load_markdown_pages(book)
    end

    private
      def create_book(user)
        Book.create(title: "The Writebook Manual", author: "37signals", everyone_access: true).tap do |book|
          with_attachment("writebook-manual.jpg") { |attachment| book.cover.attach(attachment) }
          book.update_access(readers: [], editors: [ user.id ])
        end
      end

      def load_markdown_pages(book)
        pages = {}

        Dir.glob(Rails.root.join("app/assets/markdown/demo/*.md")).each do |fname|
          front_matter = FrontMatterParser::Parser.parse_file(fname)

          if front_matter["class"] == "Section"
            load_section(book, front_matter)
          else
            page = load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
            attach_images(page)
            pages[page.leaf.slug] = page
          end
        end

        book.leaves.pages.each { |leaf| localize_ref_links(leaf.page, pages) }
      end

      def load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
        book.press(Page.new(body: front_matter.content), title: front_matter["title"]).page
      end

      def load_section(book, front_matter)
        book.press Section.new(body: front_matter.content, theme: front_matter["theme"]), title: front_matter["title"]
      end

      def attach_images(page)
        re = %r{
          \/u\/           # leading portion of path
          (\S+-\w+\.\w+)  # filename including slug and extension
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          with_attachment($1) { |attachment| page.body.uploads.attach(attachment) }

          attachment = page.body.uploads.attachments.last
          attachment.analyze

          "/u/" + attachment.slug
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

      def localize_ref_links(page, pages)
        re = %r{
          (\[.+\])              # link title
          \(                    # opening paren
          \/\d+\/[\w-]+\/\d+\/  # leading portion of path
          ([\w-]+)              # leaf slug
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          link_title, leaf_slug, anchor = $1, $2, $3
          linked_page = pages[leaf_slug]
          raise "Invalid reference link: #{page_title}" unless linked_page.present?

          url = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.leafable_slug_path(linked_page.leaf, anchor: anchor, only_path: true)

          "#{link_title}(#{url}"
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

      def with_attachment(filename)
        File.open(Rails.root.join("app/assets/images/demo/#{filename}")) do |file|
          yield io: file, filename: filename
        end
      end
  end
end

module Leaf::Editable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end
end

module Positionable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  REBALANCE_THRESHOLD = 1e-10
  ELEMENT_GAP         = 1

  included do
    scope :positioned, -> { order(:position_score, :id) }

    scope :before, ->(other) { positioned.where("position_score < ?", other.position_score) }
    scope :after,  ->(other) { positioned.where("position_score > ?", other.position_score) }

    around_create :insert_at_default_position
    after_save_commit :rebalance_positions, if: :rebalance_required?
  end

  class_methods do
    def positioned_within(parent, association:, filter:)
      define_method :positioning_parent do
        send(parent)
      end

      define_method :all_positioned_siblings do
        positioning_parent.send(association).send(filter).positioned
      end

      define_method :other_positioned_siblings do
        all_positioned_siblings.excluding(self)
      end

      private :positioning_parent, :all_positioned_siblings, :other_positioned_siblings
    end
  end

  def previous
    other_positioned_siblings.before(self).last
  end

  def next
    other_positioned_siblings.after(self).first
  end

  def move_to_position(offset, followed_by: [])
    with_positioning_lock do
      all_to_move = [ self, *followed_by ]
      before, after = before_and_after_for(offset: offset, moving: all_to_move)
      gap = (after - before) / (all_to_move.count + 1)

      all_to_move.each.with_index(1) do |item, index|
        item.update!(position_score: before + (index * gap))
      end

      remember_to_rebalance_positions if gap < REBALANCE_THRESHOLD
    end
  end

  def position_as_percentage
    100 * ordinal_position.to_f / all_positioned_siblings.count
  end

  private
    def ordinal_position
      other_positioned_siblings.before(self).count + 1
    end

    def insert_at_default_position
      with_positioning_lock do
        position_at_end
        yield
      end
    end

    def position_at_start
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)) - ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def position_at_end
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score) || 0) + ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def before_and_after_for(offset:, moving:)
      other_items = all_positioned_siblings.excluding(moving)

      if offset < 1
        after = all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)
        before = after - ELEMENT_GAP
      else
        before, after = other_items.offset(offset - 1).limit(2).pluck(:position_score)
        before ||= all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score)
        after ||= before + (moving.count.succ * ELEMENT_GAP)
      end

      [ before, after ]
    end

    def remember_to_rebalance_positions
      @rebalance_required = true
    end

    def rebalance_required?
      @rebalance_required
    end

    def rebalance_positions
      with_positioning_lock do
        odered = all_positioned_siblings.select("row_number() over (order by position_score, id) as new_score, id")
        sql = "update #{self.class.table_name} set position_score = new_score from (#{odered.to_sql}) as ordered where #{self.class.table_name}.id = ordered.id"

        self.class.connection.execute sql
      end
      @rebalance_required = false
    end

    def with_positioning_lock(&block)
      positioning_parent.with_lock &block
    end
end

module Positionable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  REBALANCE_THRESHOLD = 1e-10
  ELEMENT_GAP         = 1

  included do
    scope :positioned, -> { order(:position_score, :id) }

    scope :before, ->(other) { positioned.where("position_score < ?", other.position_score) }
    scope :after,  ->(other) { positioned.where("position_score > ?", other.position_score) }

    around_create :insert_at_default_position
    after_save_commit :rebalance_positions, if: :rebalance_required?
  end

  class_methods do
    def positioned_within(parent, association:, filter:)
      define_method :positioning_parent do
        send(parent)
      end

      define_method :all_positioned_siblings do
        positioning_parent.send(association).send(filter).positioned
      end

      define_method :other_positioned_siblings do
        all_positioned_siblings.excluding(self)
      end

      private :positioning_parent, :all_positioned_siblings, :other_positioned_siblings
    end
  end

  def previous
    other_positioned_siblings.before(self).last
  end

  def next
    other_positioned_siblings.after(self).first
  end

  def move_to_position(offset, followed_by: [])
    with_positioning_lock do
      all_to_move = [ self, *followed_by ]
      before, after = before_and_after_for(offset: offset, moving: all_to_move)
      gap = (after - before) / (all_to_move.count + 1)

      all_to_move.each.with_index(1) do |item, index|
        item.update!(position_score: before + (index * gap))
      end

      remember_to_rebalance_positions if gap < REBALANCE_THRESHOLD
    end
  end

  def position_as_percentage
    100 * ordinal_position.to_f / all_positioned_siblings.count
  end

  private
    def ordinal_position
      other_positioned_siblings.before(self).count + 1
    end

    def insert_at_default_position
      with_positioning_lock do
        position_at_end
        yield
      end
    end

    def position_at_start
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)) - ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def position_at_end
      self.position_score = (all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score) || 0) + ELEMENT_GAP
    end

    def before_and_after_for(offset:, moving:)
      other_items = all_positioned_siblings.excluding(moving)

      if offset < 1
        after = all_positioned_siblings.minimum(:position_score) || (2 * ELEMENT_GAP)
        before = after - ELEMENT_GAP
      else
        before, after = other_items.offset(offset - 1).limit(2).pluck(:position_score)
        before ||= all_positioned_siblings.maximum(:position_score)
        after ||= before + (moving.count.succ * ELEMENT_GAP)
      end

      [ before, after ]
    end

    def remember_to_rebalance_positions
      @rebalance_required = true
    end

    def rebalance_required?
      @rebalance_required
    end

    def rebalance_positions
      with_positioning_lock do
        odered = all_positioned_siblings.select("row_number() over (order by position_score, id) as new_score, id")
        sql = "update #{self.class.table_name} set position_score = new_score from (#{odered.to_sql}) as ordered where #{self.class.table_name}.id = ordered.id"

        self.class.connection.execute sql
      end
      @rebalance_required = false
    end

    def with_positioning_lock(&block)
      positioning_parent.with_lock &block
    end
end

module ActionText
  module TagHelper
    def markdown_area(record, name, value: nil, **options)
      field_name = "#{record.class.model_name.param_key}[#{name}]"
      value = record.safe_markdown_attribute(name).content.to_s if value.nil?

      data = options.delete(:data) || {}
      data.reverse_merge! \
        uploads_url: action_text_markdown_uploads_url(record_gid: record.to_signed_global_id.to_s, attribute_name: name, format: "json")

      tag.house_md value, name: field_name, data: data, **options
    end

    def house_toolbar(**options, &block)
      tag.house_md_toolbar(**options, &block)
    end

    def house_toolbar_button(action, **options, &block)
      tag.button title: action.to_s.humanize, data: { "house-md-action": action }, **options, &block
    end

    def house_toolbar_file_upload_button(name: "upload", title: "Upload File", **options, &block)
      tag.label title: title, **options do
        safe_join [
          file_field_tag(name, data: { "house-md-toolbar-file-picker": true }, style: "display: none;"),
          capture(&block)
        ]
      end
    end
  end
end

      File.basename(slug_filename, ".*").parameterize
    end

      File.extname(slug_filename).delete(".").parameterize

      slug.presence || filename.to_s

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
require File.expand_path("../../config/environment", File.dirname(__FILE__))

class Backup
  class << self
    def create
      dest = SQLite3::Database.new(backup_filename)
      backup = SQLite3::Backup.new(dest, "main", User.connection.raw_connection, "main")

      backup.step(-1)
      backup.finish
      dest.close
    end

    private
      def backup_filename
        Rails.root.join("storage", "backups").tap(&:mkpath).join(primary_database_filename)
      end

      def primary_database_filename
        path = Rails.application.config.database_configuration[Rails.env]["primary"]["database"]
        File.basename(path)
      end
  end
end

Okay, let's break this down meticulously. First, multi-tenancy is the goal, meaning we're consolidating multiple customers on a single Writebook install, and each must be segregated. I need to fully grasp the migration process and the implications of the current system.

The prompt outlines a migration strategy: creating a `tenants` table with a `name` column, and adding `tenant_id` foreign keys to the `users` and `books` tables. I need to check the existing schema conventions for table and column naming to ensure consistency, specifically in `db/migrate/` and `db/schema.rb`. I'll cross-reference with an existing table like `accounts` to be sure I am following Writebook conventions.

The plan involves moving all existing users and books to a single default tenant during the upgrade. New books, subsequently, will land within the tenant of their creator.

Now the critical detail: whether `tenant_id` can be NULL, and the implications of this. The prompt states the fixtures "name no tenant, so rows without one behave as they do today, and `bin/rails test` stays green; don't edit it." I need to unpack this carefully, reading it a few times to make sure that I understand all implications:

*   The existing fixtures (`users.yml` and `books.yml`) *do not* include a `tenant` or `tenant_id` field.
*   The directive "don't edit it" is critical. It refers to *not* modifying these existing fixtures, or changing existing tests to force the tenant relationship.
*   This suggests that `tenant_id` on both `users` and `books` *must* be nullable, or the tests will break with NOT NULL constraint failures or validation errors. If the `tenant_id` field weren't nullable, the existing fixture data would fail.
*   I can *add* new test files for tenant-specific behavior (e.g., `test/models/tenant_test.rb`), but I cannot change existing test files or fixtures. I need to be sure that the default tenant can be `nil`.
*   The "don't edit it" phrase also applies to `bin/rails test`.
*   The goal is to maintain backward compatibility, ensuring existing code and tests continue to function as they do now while enabling multi-tenancy.

The focus is on not breaking existing functionality during the transition. I will be sure to add the ability to use a nil tenant, while making the tenant column nullable. I need to plan for both migration and backward compatibility. This will greatly inform my implementation strategy.

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing Book Creation and Tenant Association in Writebook**

Okay, here's what I'm thinking, based on this grep output and code analysis. My focus is on how new `Book` objects are created and how they get associated with a `tenant`.

First, the grep output is helpful, showing every `Book` reference in `app/`. The key area to examine is `BooksController#create`. I see that in both `new` and `create` actions, we're dealing with `Book` creation and that the tenant association is likely the crux of the problem.

Let's break down `BooksController#create`:

I notice the line `book = Book.create! book_params.merge(tenant: Current.user.tenant)`. This is where the tenant assignment happens. But then I saw that we *could* have a default on the `Book` itself!

Now, if `Book` has `belongs_to :tenant, optional: true, default: -> { Current.user&.tenant }`, things change. In the `BooksController#new` action, `Book.new` would automatically get the `tenant` attribute from `Current.user`. And in `BooksController#create`, `Book.create!` would also automatically get the `tenant` attribute from `Current.user`.

However, the tricky part lies in testing. We need to consider scenarios where `Current.user` *isn't* set or is set differently in our tests. For instance, what if we have a test where `Current.user = user_a`, and then we call `Book.create!(title: "Foo", tenant: tenant_b)`? Or, what about a test where we *don't* pass a `tenant` at all, expecting `tenant_id: nil`, but instead, the `default` kicks in and assigns the `tenant` of `Current.user`?

Thinking about integration tests, specifically, after the `sign_in :user_a` call, `Current.user` might still be set, or it might be reset. I need to know precisely when `Current.user` is reset by the `ActionDispatch::Executor`.

What if in a model test someone explicitly sets `Current.user = user_a`, and then calls `Book.create!(title: "Untenanted")` expecting `tenant_id: nil` vs expecting `user_a.tenant`?

The prompt says "New books land in their creator's tenant", which means I need to double-check every place where a "creator" is referenced when creating a `Book`. I found this in `BooksController#create` (`app/views/books/new.html.erb` shows `creating_user: Current.user`), and `DemoContent.create_manual(user)` which takes a `user` and creates a `Book` with `tenant: user.tenant`! This setup ensures the manual lands in the `user`'s tenant if it exists.

Now, I'm going to look carefully at the interaction of `belongs_to :tenant, optional: true` vs. the `default` value assignment. The key is that the tests themselves need to be very precise about their setup and the expectations around `Current.user`.

Let's test this in `bin/rails runner` to see how `Current.user` behaves! Never guess how `Current.user` behaves in `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest`!

**My Analysis of Tenant Isolation in Writebook**

Alright, let's break this down. My goal is to ensure that users can only access data within their designated tenant, or publicly published data.

First, the core principle: If a user is signed in, I need to ensure they can only access books and related content (pages, edits, etc.) belonging to their tenant. If they are not signed in, they should only be able to see published content.

Key areas to consider:

*   **`same_tenant?` Definition:** This is crucial. If `same_tenant?(user)` is defined as `user.present? && user.tenant_id == tenant_id`, then a `nil` user (signed-out visitor) correctly results in `false`. This keeps out all signed-out visitors. The important part is making sure this always works, including when `user.tenant_id` or `book.tenant_id` are `nil`.
*   **Book Creation and Access:** In `BooksController#new`, I'll need to set the `@book.tenant_id` correctly. Setting `@book = Book.new(tenant: Current.user.tenant)` or using a `belongs_to :tenant, optional: true, default: -> { Current.user&.tenant }` on the `Book` model will ensure new books are tied to the current user's tenant from the get-go.
*   **Routing and Controllers Audit:**
    *   **`/` (BooksController#index):** This is tricky. I need to make sure the book index respects tenant separation. `Book.accessable_or_published` needs to be scoped correctly to the current user's tenant (or public if signed out). The caching mechanism, which uses `[ @books, signed_in? ]`, will work because the SQL query will differ based on the tenant. Critically, if `signed_in?` is false and no books are published, the app redirects to the login screen. Otherwise, it shows the published books.
    *   **`/books/new` and `/books`: (BooksController):** The creation flow must ensure the book's `tenant_id` is set to the current user's tenant. `update_accesses` also needs to respect tenant boundaries.
    *   **`/:id/:slug` (BooksController#show):** This is a key control point. Even if `allow_unauthenticated_access` runs and restores the current user, `Book.accessable_or_published` must filter to the proper tenant. Requesting a book from a different tenant will result in an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` (404), ensuring isolation. Also, the same is true for the markdown version (`.md`).
    *   **`edit`, `update`, `destroy` (BooksController):**  Ensuring that unauthorized access also leads to a 404 is important. The `set_book` runs *before* the access check (`ensure_editable`), so unauthorized requests result in 404s.
    *   **Nested Resources (e.g., `Books::PublicationsController`, `Books::BookmarksController`, `Books::Leaves::MovesController`, `Books::SearchesController`, `PagesController`, `SectionsController`, etc.)**:  I need to apply the tenant scope at the *beginning* of *every* `before_action` that involves a book or leaf, using `Book.accessable_or_published`. The concern `SetBookLeaf` is key, running `set_book` *before* `set_leaf`. This includes the ActionText markdown upload route (`/uploads`, `/u/*slug`). If an unauthorized user tries to access these resources, a 404 is served (even those requiring signed-in users), instead of a 403.
    *   **`Pages::EditsController`**: This one uses a different URL pattern, `/pages/:page_id/edits/:id`. This route needs `Current.user.leaves` in scope, ensuring that a user can *only* access edits related to their books.
*   **ActionCable and Turbo Streams**: There are no custom channels, so that's simple enough. The Turbo Streams should respect the scope.
*   **UsersController & Related:**  The user and profile routes must remain public, but the `tenant_id` on new user creation (e.g., via `/join/:join_code`) must be considered. In particular, existing `User#grant_access_to_everyone_books` code should not grant access to other tenants, or it may expose their data.
*   **`FirstRun` and `DemoContent`**: When creating demo content, the books created must be correctly scoped to the tenant.

**Tenant Creation Logic Deep Dive**

Okay, so I'm looking closely at how `FirstRun` handles user creation, specifically within `FirstRun.create!(user_params)`. The key question is, should `FirstRun` automatically create a `Tenant` during the initial setup? Wait, this is crucial... what if someone joins the system *later* using a join code via `/join/:join_code` in `UsersController#create` on a single-tenant setup started with `FirstRun`?

Here's the problem: If `FirstRun` creates a `Tenant` for the first user, then `User.first` (and therefore, the initial owner of *The Writebook Manual*) would have `tenant_id = 1`. Then a new user invited with a join code would have `tenant_id = nil`, which means they wouldn't have access to *The Writebook Manual* or the original user's content! They'd be siloed off, which is the opposite of what we want.

But, if `FirstRun.create!` *doesn't* create a `Tenant` unless the `user_params` specifically include `tenant:` or `tenant_id:`, then:

*   Both the initial user *and* anyone joining via `/join/:join_code` in a fresh single-tenant install *both* have `tenant_id = nil`. The existing behavior would continue to work!
*   And, within `DemoContent.create_book(user)`, passing `tenant: user.tenant` would mean if `DemoContent.create_manual(user)` *is* called for a user with a tenant, the manual ends up in the correct tenant. If `user.tenant` is `nil`, the manual has `tenant: nil`. This is cohesive!

This looks like a solid and consistent approach, and the key is that `tenant_id` needs to remain `nil` unless a new tenant is created, or a user is added to an existing tenant.

Now, I've got to check *everything* else to make sure there are no subtle interactions or unexpected behavior. Time to audit all the tests, views, and models that might touch this area. I'm going to read through `test/controllers/pictures_controller_test.rb`, `test/controllers/sections_controller_test.rb`, `test/system/edit_page_test.rb`, `test/system/publish_book_test.rb`, and `app/views/leaves/*` carefully. I have to make sure nothing breaks or has unexpected behavior. This is going to be good.

module Book::Accessable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
    scope :with_everyone_access, -> { where(everyone_access: true) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def accessable_or_published(user: Current.user)
      if user.present?
        accessable_or_published_books(user: user)
      else
        published
      end
    end

    def accessable_or_published_books(user: Current.user)
      where(id: user.books).or(published).where(tenant_id: user.tenant_id)
    end
  end

  def accessable?(user: Current.user)
    same_tenant?(user) && accesses.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def editable?(user: Current.user)
    same_tenant?(user) && (access_for(user: user)&.editor? || user.administrator?)
  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user) if same_tenant?(user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    tenant_user_ids = User.where(tenant_id: tenant_id).ids.to_set
    editors = Set.new(editors.map(&:to_i)) & tenant_user_ids
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.where(tenant_id: tenant_id).ids : readers.map(&:to_i)) & tenant_user_ids

    all = editors + readers
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ]) if all_accesses.any?
    accesses.where.not(user_id: all).delete_all
  end

  private
    def same_tenant?(user)
      user.present? && user.tenant_id == tenant_id
    end
end
EOF

class DemoContent
  class << self
    def create_manual(user)
      book = create_book(user)
      load_markdown_pages(book)
    end

    private
      def create_book(user)
        Book.create(title: "The Writebook Manual", author: "37signals", everyone_access: true, tenant: user.tenant).tap do |book|
          with_attachment("writebook-manual.jpg") { |attachment| book.cover.attach(attachment) }
          book.update_access(readers: [], editors: [ user.id ])
        end
      end

      def load_markdown_pages(book)
        pages = {}

        Dir.glob(Rails.root.join("app/assets/markdown/demo/*.md")).each do |fname|
          front_matter = FrontMatterParser::Parser.parse_file(fname)

          if front_matter["class"] == "Section"
            load_section(book, front_matter)
          else
            page = load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
            attach_images(page)
            pages[page.leaf.slug] = page
          end
        end

        book.leaves.pages.each { |leaf| localize_ref_links(leaf.page, pages) }
      end

      def load_markdown_page(book, front_matter)
        book.press(Page.new(body: front_matter.content), title: front_matter["title"]).page
      end

      def load_section(book, front_matter)
        book.press Section.new(body: front_matter.content, theme: front_matter["theme"]), title: front_matter["title"]
      end

      def attach_images(page)
        re = %r{
          \/u\/           # leading portion of path
          (\S+-\w+\.\w+)  # filename including slug and extension
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          with_attachment($1) { |attachment| page.body.uploads.attach(attachment) }

          attachment = page.body.uploads.attachments.last
          attachment.analyze

          "/u/" + attachment.slug
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

      def localize_ref_links(page, pages)
        re = %r{
          (\[.+\])              # link title
          \(                    # opening paren
          \/\d+\/[\w-]+\/\d+\/  # leading portion of path
          ([\w-]+)              # leaf slug
        }x

        body = page.body.content.gsub(re) do |match|
          link_title, leaf_slug, anchor = $1, $2, $3
          linked_page = pages[leaf_slug]
          raise "Invalid reference link: #{page_title}" unless linked_page.present?

          url = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.leafable_slug_path(linked_page.leaf, anchor: anchor, only_path: true)

          "#{link_title}(#{url}"
        end

        page.update!(body: body)
      end

      def with_attachment(filename)
        File.open(Rails.root.join("app/assets/images/demo/#{filename}")) do |file|
          yield io: file, filename: filename
        end
      end
  end
end
EOF

class BooksController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access only: %i[ index show ]

  before_action :set_book, only: %i[ show edit update destroy ]

  end

    update_accesses(book)

    redirect_to book_slug_url(book)
  end

  def show
    @leaves = @book.leaves.active.with_leafables.positioned

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html
      format.md
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    @book.update(book_params)
    update_accesses(@book)
    remove_cover if params[:remove_cover] == "true"

    redirect_to book_slug_url(@book)
  end

  def destroy
    @book.destroy

    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_book
      @book = Book.accessable_or_published.find params[:id]
    end

    def set_users
      @users = User.active.where(tenant_id: Current.user.tenant_id).ordered
    end

    def ensure_editable

        require_authentication
      end

    end

    def update_accesses(book)
      editors = [ Current.user.id, *params[:editor_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]
      readers = [ Current.user.id, *params[:reader_ids]&.map(&:to_i) ]

      book.update_access(editors: editors, readers: readers)

      @book.cover.purge
    end
end

class ActionText::Markdown::UploadsController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access only: :show

  before_action do
    ActiveStorage::Current.url_options = { protocol: request.protocol, host: request.host, port: request.port }
  end

  def create
    @record = GlobalID::Locator.locate_signed params[:record_gid]
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound if @record.nil? || (@record.respond_to?(:book) && @record.book && @record.book.tenant_id != Current.user.tenant_id)

    @markdown = @record.safe_markdown_attribute params[:attribute_name]
    @markdown.uploads.attach [ params[:file] ]
    @markdown.save!

    @upload = @markdown.uploads.attachments.last

    render :create, status: :created, formats: :json
  end

  def show
    @attachment = ActiveStorage::Attachment.find_by! slug: "#{params[:slug]}.#{params[:format]}"
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound if signed_in? && (book = book_for_attachment(@attachment)) && book.tenant_id != Current.user.tenant_id

    expires_in 1.year, public: true
    redirect_to @attachment.url
  end

  private
    def book_for_attachment(attachment)
      record = attachment.record
      leafable = record.is_a?(ActionText::Markdown) ? record.record : record
      leafable&.try(:book) || (Edit.find_by(leafable: leafable)&.leaf&.book if leafable)
    end
end

First, let's nail down an *in-place upgrade* scenario. I'll meticulously test rolling back the migration to a pre-migration state, populate the database with accounts, users, books, and various associations, *then* run the migration and meticulously verify the tenant creation and assignment. I'll specifically confirm the tenant's creation, the data integrity (names, timestamps), the tenant ID assignment to existing records, and full access for all users. I also need to test a case where there are no existing accounts when running the migration, to verify the new account is created correctly.

If the migration were to create a tenant row on an empty DB, the test DB would be corrupted and I'd encounter flaky, unreliable Minitest results. That's a great catch!

Let's start with scenarios regarding page edits. If I request a page edit history (`/pages/:page_leaf_id/edits/latest`), what happens if the leaf is in another tenant and has no edits? Or, what happens if a page has been trashed? I need to trace the code to confirm that no unexpected errors or data leaks will occur. This is about making sure users always get a clear and secure 404.

Next, I need to test access control. Let's make sure the role-based access control works as intended in various cases: members vs administrators; users with and without access rows; and published vs. unpublished books. I'm going to set up very specific tests for each of these permutations to ensure the logic and permissions are respected.

Finally, I need to test that `Book` loading in the DB works as expected in edge cases. Remember the default value in `Book` model? What if `tenant_id` is null in the DB row? I need to confirm that `Current.user` doesn't *interfere* with the `Book.find(...)` when retrieving data. If it did, it would create an impossible situation! require "test_helper"

class TenantsEdgeCasesTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  test "loading NULL tenant_id book from DB while Current.user has a tenant keeps tenant_id nil" do
    tenant_a = Tenant.create!(name: "Customer A")
    alice = User.create!(name: "Alice", email_address: "alice@a.com", password: "secret123456", tenant: tenant_a)

    Current.user = alice
    reloaded_handbook = Book.find(books(:handbook).id)
    assert_nil reloaded_handbook.tenant_id
    assert_nil reloaded_handbook.tenant
    assert_not reloaded_handbook.accessable?(user: alice)
    assert_not reloaded_handbook.editable?(user: alice)

    # New book without explicit tenant gets Current.user.tenant
    new_book = Book.create!(title: "Auto Tenant Book")
    assert_equal tenant_a, new_book.tenant

    # New book with explicit nil tenant keeps nil tenant
    nil_book = Book.create!(title: "Explicit Nil Book", tenant: nil)
    assert_nil nil_book.tenant_id

    # New book with explicit other tenant gets other tenant
    tenant_b = Tenant.create!(name: "Customer B")
    other_book = Book.create!(title: "Explicit B Book", tenant: tenant_b)
    assert_equal tenant_b, other_book.tenant
  ensure
    Current.reset
  end

  test "migration sweeps existing users and books into one tenant and is reversible" do
    require Rails.root.join("db/migrate/20261120223500_create_tenants.rb")

    # Ensure fixtures exist in DB (4 users, 2 books, 1 account '37signals')
    assert_equal 4, User.count
    assert_equal 2, Book.count
    assert_equal "37signals", Account.first.name

    CreateTenants.migrate(:down)
    User.reset_column_information
    Book.reset_column_information

    assert_not_includes User.column_names, "tenant_id"
    assert_not_includes Book.column_names, "tenant_id"
    assert_not ActiveRecord::Base.connection.table_exists?(:tenants)

    CreateTenants.migrate(:up)
    Tenant.reset_column_information
    User.reset_column_information
    Book.reset_column_information

    assert_equal 1, Tenant.count
    tenant = Tenant.first
    assert_equal "37signals", tenant.name
    assert_equal [ tenant.id ], User.pluck(:tenant_id).uniq
    assert_equal [ tenant.id ], Book.pluck(:tenant_id).uniq

    # Also test when no Account row exists!
    Account.delete_all
    CreateTenants.migrate(:down)
    CreateTenants.migrate(:up)
    Tenant.reset_column_information
    User.reset_column_information
    Book.reset_column_information

    assert_equal 1, Tenant.count
    tenant2 = Tenant.first
    assert_equal "Writebook", tenant2.name
    assert_equal [ tenant2.id ], User.pluck(:tenant_id).uniq
    assert_equal [ tenant2.id ], Book.pluck(:tenant_id).uniq
  end

  test "cross-tenant isolation for member with reader access, member with no access, and nil-tenant user vs tenanted book" do
    tenant_a = Tenant.create!(name: "Customer A")
    tenant_b = Tenant.create!(name: "Customer B")

    member_a = User.create!(name: "Member A", email_address: "ma@a.com", password: "secret123456", role: :member, tenant: tenant_a)
    admin_b = User.create!(name: "Admin B", email_address: "ab@b.com", password: "secret123456", role: :administrator, tenant: tenant_b)

    book_b_pub = Book.create!(title: "B Published", published: true, everyone_access: true, tenant: tenant_b)
    book_b_unpub = Book.create!(title: "B Unpublished", published: false, everyone_access: true, tenant: tenant_b)

    leaf_b_no_edits = book_b_pub.press Page.new(body: "No edits yet"), title: "Fresh B Page"
    leaf_b_trashed = book_b_pub.press Page.new(body: "Trashed content"), title: "Trashed B Page"
    leaf_b_trashed.trashed!

    # Markdown upload on leaf_b_no_edits
    md = leaf_b_no_edits.page.body.tap(&:save!)
    md.uploads.attach fixture_file_upload("reading.webp", "image/webp")
    upload_b = md.uploads.last

    # Give reader access rows across tenants (simulating pilot merge)
    Access.create!(user: member_a, book: book_b_pub, level: :reader)
    Access.create!(user: member_a, book: book_b_unpub, level: :reader)
    Access.create!(user: users(:kevin), book: book_b_pub, level: :reader)

    # Test member_a
    sign_in member_a
    get root_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_not_in_body "B Published"
    assert_not_in_body "B Unpublished"

    get book_slug_path(book_b_pub)
    assert_response :not_found

    get book_slug_path(book_b_unpub)
    assert_response :not_found

    get leafable_slug_path(leaf_b_no_edits)
    assert_response :not_found

    get page_edit_path(leaf_b_no_edits, "latest")
    assert_response :not_found

    get page_edit_path(leaf_b_trashed, "latest")
    assert_response :not_found

    get action_text_markdown_upload_path(slug: upload_b.slug)
    assert_response :not_found

    post action_text_markdown_uploads_path, params: {
      record_gid: leaf_b_no_edits.page.to_signed_global_id.to_s,
      attribute_name: "body",
      file: fixture_file_upload("reading.webp", "image/webp")
    }, as: :xhr
    assert_response :not_found

    # Attempt to pass cross-tenant user IDs in book creation/update
    post books_path, params: {
      book: { title: "A Book", everyone_access: false },
      "editor_ids[]": admin_b.id,
      "reader_ids[]": users(:kevin).id
    }
    book_a = Book.order(:id).last
    assert_equal tenant_a, book_a.tenant
    assert_not Access.exists?(user: admin_b, book: book_a)
    assert_not Access.exists?(user: users(:kevin), book: book_a)
    assert Access.exists?(user: member_a, book: book_a)

    # Nil-tenant user (kevin) also cannot see Tenant B books even with Access row & published: true
    sign_out
    sign_in :kevin
    get root_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body "Handbook"
    assert_not_in_body "B Published"

    get book_slug_path(book_b_pub)
    assert_response :not_found

    get leafable_slug_path(leaf_b_no_edits)
    assert_response :not_found

    get page_edit_path(leaf_b_trashed, "latest")
    assert_response :not_found
    assert cookies[:session_token].present?
  end

  test "DemoContent creates manual in creator's tenant" do
    tenant_a = Tenant.create!(name: "Customer A")
    alice = User.create!(name: "Alice", email_address: "alice@a.com", password: "secret123456", role: :administrator, tenant: tenant_a)
    DemoContent.create_manual(alice)

    manual = Book.where(title: "The Writebook Manual", tenant: tenant_a).first
    assert_not_nil manual
    assert manual.editable?(user: alice)
  end
end
EOF

messages.content:
I have implemented multi-tenant isolation for Writebook:

1. **Migration & Schema (`db/migrate/20261120223500_create_tenants.rb`, `db/schema.rb`, `app/models/tenant.rb`)**:
   - Created the `tenants` table (`name`, `null: false`, timestamps) and `Tenant` model (`has_many :users` and `has_many :books`).
   - Added nullable `tenant_id` foreign keys on `users` and `books`.
   - Swept all existing users and books into a single tenant during migration so running installs upgrade in place, while leaving rows without a tenant (`tenant_id: nil`) valid so fixtures and tenantless records continue to behave as before.

2. **Creator Tenant Assignment (`app/models/book.rb`, `app/models/current.rb`, `app/models/demo_content.rb`)**:
   - Associated `User` and `Book` with `belongs_to :tenant, optional: true`.
   - Defaulted `Book#tenant_id` to `Current.user&.tenant_id` (and passed `user.tenant` in `DemoContent.create_manual`) so new books land in their creator's tenant.

3. **Tenant Isolation & Access Control (`app/models/book/accessable.rb`, `app/models/user.rb`, `app/controllers/books_controller.rb`, `app/controllers/action_text/markdown/uploads_controller.rb`)**:
   - Scoped `User#books` (and `User#leaves` through `books`) and `Book.accessable_or_published`, `Book#accessable?`, `Book#editable?`, and `Book#access_for` to matching `tenant_id` for signed-in users, ensuring cross-tenant books (published or not, and even with pre-existing `Access` rows or administrator roles) never appear in the library and answer `404 Not Found` across all book, leafable/page/section/picture, upload, and edit-history endpoints while keeping the user signed in.
   - Left signed-out access to all published books across tenants and `/users` unchanged.
   - Scoped `everyone_access` reader grants (`Book#update_access` and `User#grant_access_to_everyone_books`) and book-form user lists (`BooksController#set_users`) to the same tenant.

I am now ready to complete the task and submit the final output.
